      children: "> **Beta:** Paragraph is available as a beta component. Its API and visual design may change before the stable release.\n\nFor installation and configuration, see [`@db-ux/ngx-core-components`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@db-ux/ngx-core-components).\n\n`db-paragraph` renders a `p` for block-level body copy. For inline text inside a sentence use a plain `span`, there is no component for it. Spacing between several paragraphs belongs to [`db-text-group`](?path=/docs/components-dbtextgroup-overview--docs).\n\n### Load the component\n\n```ts\nimport { Component } from \"@angular/core\";\nimport { DBParagraph } from \"@db-ux/ngx-core-components\";\n\n@Component({\n\tselector: \"app-example\",\n\timports: [DBParagraph],\n\tstandalone: true,\n\ttemplateUrl: \"./example.component.html\"\n})\nexport class ExampleComponent {}\n```\n\n```html\n<db-paragraph>A paragraph of body copy.</db-paragraph>\n<db-paragraph size=\"sm\">\n\tA smaller paragraph with an <span>inline passage</span>.\n</db-paragraph>\n```\n\n### Size\n\n`size` accepts `lg`, `md` and `sm` and has **no default**: omitting it inherits the size from the surrounding typography.\n\nIn a default context that is the same as `md`, because the foundations set the root to the medium step - an unset paragraph measures 16px with a 24px line height, exactly like `size=\"md\"`. The difference only shows inside a container that changed the type scale, where an unset paragraph follows it and a fixed `md` would not. Density tokens provide responsive typography, so there is no breakpoint-specific size input.\n\n### Font weight\n\nThere is no font-weight property. Emphasis is semantic and belongs to the element, so use `strong` inside the paragraph. That works at any size, because the weight sits on the `strong` rather than on the paragraph:\n\n```html\n<db-paragraph>\n\tA paragraph with an <strong>emphasised passage</strong>.\n</db-paragraph>\n```\n\nFor a presentational weight on the whole paragraph the foundations' global `data-font` annotation covers `digital` (300), `regular` (400), `medium` (500), `semibold` (600) and `bold` (700). It is forwarded like any other `data-*` attribute, but it only takes effect while `size` is unset: a set size applies the `font` shorthand at a higher specificity and resets the weight. Measured, `data-font=\"bold\"` alone computes to 700, and combined with `size=\"sm\"` it falls back to 400.\n\n### Spacing and alignment\n\n`db-paragraph` renders a `p`, so block spacing comes from the foundations' `data-text-spacing` opt-in: with the attribute on the element or any ancestor it gets `0.5lh` above and below, without it anywhere above it renders flush, and `data-text-spacing=\"false\"` switches it back off. A surrounding [`db-text-group`](?path=/docs/components-dbtextgroup-overview--docs) sets that attribute for a whole block.\n\nThere is deliberately no `text-align`, which is what lets the `alignment` of a `db-text-group` reach the paragraph by inheritance.\n\n### Content, attributes and accessibility\n\nContent always comes through the default content, there is no `text` input.\n\n`db-paragraph` renders a `p`, which is flow content, so it fits in `dd`, `figcaption`, `blockquote`, `li` and `td`, but **not** in `legend`, `label`, `summary` or `button`. Use a `span` there.\n\nBody copy gets `text-wrap: pretty`, the counterpart to `text-wrap: balance` on headings. It is a progressive enhancement: browsers without support compute `wrap`.\n\nStandard `aria-*`, `data-*`, `role`, `title`, `class` and `style` attributes are forwarded from the host element to the rendered element. It stays on the `<db-paragraph>` host, which the `<p>` inherits it from, so rendering and assistive technology are unaffected but a selector such as `p[lang]` does not match.\n\n`id` is a regular input, not a forwarded attribute, and is rendered on the element."
